<MethodEndpoint
  method={"put"}
  path={"/organizations/{organizationId}/users/{userId}/deactivate"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Deactivates credentials so that they can't connect.

Nothing is deleted: the password, SSH keys, home directory and network rules are kept, and
activating the credentials restores access as it was. Sessions already open aren't ended.

To respond to a suspected leak, deactivate the credentials, then rotate the password and remove
any SSH key you don't trust before you activate them again. Deactivating doesn't revoke S3
access keys attached to the credentials.
